summary: The note traces McDonald's pioneering role in fast-food breakfast. It describes the 1972 introduction of the Egg McMuffin, based on market research suggesting consumers would welcome a quick breakfast, and the later expansion to a full breakfast line in 1975, first tested in locations such as New York City. It also notes that by 1987 McDonald's supplied one-fourth of all breakfasts eaten out in the United States.
one_line: Overview of how McDonald's pioneered fast-food breakfast with the Egg McMuffin in 1972 and expanded to a full breakfast line.
key_facts: McDonald's pioneered breakfast fast food with the introduction of the Egg McMuffin in 1972.
The Egg McMuffin was introduced in 1972 after market research indicated that a quick breakfast would be welcomed by consumers.
Five years after the Egg McMuffin, McDonald's added a full breakfast line to its menu.
McDonald's added a full breakfast line to its menus in 1975.
In test market locations such as New York City, McDonald's added a full breakfast line to its menus in 1975.
By 1987, one-fourth of all breakfasts eaten out in the United States came from McDonald's restaurants.
